Apparently lean4lean caught this proof of false that the lean kernel and nanoda failed to catch.

https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/14807

We claim that lean4lean, another implementation of the Lean kernel, does not have this bug, since their isProp already uses ensureSortCore (See https://github.com/digama0/lean4lean/blob/master/Lean4Lean/TypeChecker.lean#L224-L230).

that's a really interesting bug, since it implies that it's not the case that inferType e returns something the whnfs to sort u, which I'm pretty sure I proved must happen :upside_down: Maybe it's exploiting nontransitivity somehow?
A very helpful digest of what goes wrong: https://gist.github.com/blume0/2f083ef60f9ccb8c961e888207e47ff7. Indeed non-transitivity is involved!

Haha non-transitivity was on the list of smelly things that scared me and just a few days ago someone was doubting it impacted soundness (I think it was @Jason Rute actually) even though it felt to me like it probably did

Oh, I didn't notice this thread when creating #lean4 > Human understanding of the soundness bug with `is_prop` . Any thoughts on the second question there (might there be other instances of this, in particular with separating parameters from indices)?

@Talia Ringer yes, I did say that and I guess I was wrong. I was mislead by the mathematical proof that nontransitivity was sound and the “party line” that it was fine to have it in Lean (again because it was proved sound). Anyway, hopefully in a few months or so we will have a verified kernel and then we won’t have to have these debates (either because there is no more non-transitivity or because the kernel is proven sound).
@Jason Rute No more non-transitivity? How would that work?
Well, for one, banning @Quot Prop perhaps. It's totally useless, removing it breaks nothing, and causes an intransitivity bug.

My opinion (also mentioned on the PR) is that the approach taken in the PR to try to fix determinism is a red herring, and instead the problem is that we check projection legality at every use site instead of once and for all, and it also uses some computed metadata which it can end up computing inconsistently if some things don't reduce. I think it should just be more robust with respect to defeq failures: it's okay that sometimes isDefEq fails on valid things, as long as this is uniformly underapproximating all typing judgments and does not lead to actual branching to things that might not hold. This is especially true when it comes to determining the shape of an inductive - the arity of the type and constructors, the sort annotations, where it nested-recurses

Jeremy Chen said :

Well, for one, banning @Quot Prop perhaps. It's totally useless, removing it breaks nothing, and causes an intransitivity bug.

Right. What about the computation rule of Acc.rec?

Mario Carneiro said :

This is especially true when it comes to determining the shape of an inductive - the arity of the type and constructors, the sort annotations, where it nested-recurses

So, do you think there might be more proofs of False from non-stability of these things under substitution?

Jean Abou Samra said:

Jason Rute No more non-transitivity? How would that work?

In effect, all the fixes needed to have a transitive equality are known, it's a matter of testing them robustly enough, and integrating them in the kernel, namely:

  • some incompletenesses around the implementation of structure eta and eta-for-unit have been known for a while and are fixable with little to no issue
  • Quots of propositions should not themselves be propositions, this is what your repro of the soundness bug used to break transitivity
  • Acc should not largely eliminate. A "nice" type-theoretic solution studied here is to make its iota rule propositional rather than definitional, another easier solution explored in lean is to simply not largely eliminate recursive predicates in the kernel, and (ab)use the axiom of choice to recover the theoretical strength offered by Acc (lean4#13851).

Fix all this and Lean should, modulo undiscovered implementation bugs, have a transitive defeq for good :)
Thanks for the very useful summary @Arthur Adjedj! Has Lean FRO expressed an interested in eventually making these changes?
I think you'll have to wait for Lean 5 for that to happen
Or maybe Lean .*5.*?
Ah, 4.35.0. The FRO is quick it seems.
@Jeremy Chen link?
Sorry it wasn't clear, it was a joke about 4.35.0 matching the regex .*5.* in the previous message
Heh, ok

@Jeremy Chen from this blog post

Starting with Lean v4.35.0, we will include the command lake check. This command will export and recheck the project using lean4checker. We are planning to include the nanoda, lean-inductive-models, and lean4lean kernels in the official Lean distribution.

So if Lean4lean can get the changes faster than the official kernel I guess that counts?

I assume such changes would require a change to the libraries, right? Given that it is a change to the type theory and axioms? (Although maybe such a refactor is small.). If so, kernels would have to uniformly change all at once, right?
